paper.title: DTR Bandit: Learning to Make Response-Adaptive Decisions With Low Regret

settings.name_in_paper: Two-armed two-stage DTR bandit with linear Q-functions
settings.out_of_scope_reason: Two-stage dynamic treatment regime problem in which the first-stage action affects the second-stage context: effectively a two-step episodic RL problem with linear Q-functions.
unmapped: two stages per round: the first-stage action changes the second-stage context (state transition)
Q-functions are linear in known feature maps psi_m with ||psi_m|| <= x_max and ||beta_{a,m}|| <= b_max
margin condition on the Q-function differences in both stages with exponents alpha_1, alpha_2 (alpha = min)
positive-definite design matrices on regions where each arm is optimal by margin Delta_m (Assumption 3)
the learner knows the diversity margins Delta_1, Delta_2 and a forced-sampling parameter q >= C_tilde, which depends on sigma, phi_m, x_max, d
settings.definition_quote: nature draws a potential trajectory $\braces{\bx_{t,1}, \bx_{t,2}\prns{a_1}, \bx_{t,3}\prns{a_1, a_2}}_{a_1\in[2], a_2\in[2]}$ i.i.d. from a fixed but unknown distribution $\mathcal{P}$. In the first stage of each round, the decision maker observes the initial context $\bx_{t,1}$ and pulls an arm $A_{t,1}\in [2]$ ... They then obtain an updated context $\bx_{t,2} = \bx_{t,2}(A_{t,1})$. In the second stage, the decision maker pulls an arm $A_{t,2}\in [2]$ ...

settings.out_of_scope_reason: Two-stage dynamic treatment regime problem (two-step episodic RL with linear Q-functions), here with delayed observations.
unmapped: two stages per round with an action-dependent second-stage context
linear Q-functions, margin condition (alpha_1, alpha_2), diversity assumption as in the undelayed setting
the interarrival times and second-stage delays are i.i.d. sub-exponential (means mu_1, mu_2; parameters (nu_1, b_1), (nu_2, b_2))
the learner knows Delta_1, Delta_2 and q >= C_tilde
settings.definition_quote: Assume that first stage observations arrive in intervals $I_t^1$, which are i.i.d. non-negative sub-exponential random variables with mean $\mu_1$ and parameters $(\nu_1, b_1)$. ... assume for the $t$-th unit we observe the second stage context with a delay of $I_t^2$ after its first-stage arrival, where $I_t^2$ are i.i.d. non-negative sub-exponential random variables with mean $\mu_2$ and parameters $(\nu_2, b_2)$.

algorithms.name: DTRBandit
requires_knowledge_of: q >= C_tilde (depends on sigma, phi_m, x_max, d)

bound.expression_latex: O( d^{\frac{\alpha+1}{2}}(\log d)^{\frac{\alpha+2}{2}} T^{\frac{1-\alpha}{2}} +  d \log d \log T + (d\log d)^2)

conditions: Assumption 1: linear Q-functions with ||psi_m|| <= x_max, ||beta_{a,m}|| <= b_max, sigma-sub-Gaussian residues
Assumption 2: margin condition with exponents alpha_1, alpha_2 and constants gamma_1, gamma_2
Assumption 3: positive-definite design matrices in the regions where each arm is optimal by margin Delta_m (phi_1, phi_2)
tuning: q >= C_tilde (explicitly q >= C_tilde_1 v C_tilde_2)

source.label: thm: regret upper bound
source.quote: Suppose \cref{assumption: bounded,assumption: margin,assumption: diversity} hold. Then there exists a constant $\tilde{C}$ such that, if $q\ge \tilde{C}$, then the expected regret of our algorithm is bounded as follows: ... O( d^{\frac{\alpha+1}{2}}(\log d)^{\frac{\alpha+2}{2}} T^{\frac{1-\alpha}{2}} +  d \log d \log T + (d\log d)^2),& \alpha <1

results.notes: Regret is defined through differences of expected rewards, so pseudo_regret. The theorem also gives an explicit non-asymptotic bound with constants (not recorded separately because of piecewise indicator functions). The constants hidden by O depend on x_max, b_max, sigma, phi_m, gamma_m and Delta_m.

conditions: Assumption 1: linear Q-functions with ||psi_m|| <= x_max, ||beta_{a,m}|| <= b_max, sigma-sub-Gaussian residues
Assumption 2: margin condition with exponent alpha = min(alpha_1, alpha_2) = 1
Assumption 3: positive-definite design matrices on the margin regions
results.notes: This is the main logarithmic-regret case; by Lemma 1, alpha = 1 holds for bounded densities.

symbols.b_2: sub-exponential parameter b of the delays
